title: First-Call Experience: Labs, Quickstarts, and Error Recovery Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is a practical playbook for the "first-call" developer experience when a user installs an SDK/CLI and invokes a Redwood API for the first time. It combines short guided labs (worksheets for a 10–30 minute hands-on flow), a minimal quickstart for both Node and Python, and an error-recovery checklist that support engineers and docs writers can reference. Goal is to reduce time-to-value to under 10 minutes for simple text generation and under 20 minutes for streaming/chat + function-calling flows.

Audience:
- New developers evaluating Redwood hosted API or migrating to Redwood Dedicated/Private
- Internal engs who write quickstarts, SDKs, or onboarding labs
- Solutions engineers doing live demos

Key outcomes we measure from this playbook:
- Median time from signup to successful first API call (target < 10min)
- % of first-time runs that complete without an error (target > 90%)
- Common error modes surfaced to SRE/SDK triage (auto-filed)

Top-level approach (TL;DR):
- Provide a single-file minimal quickstart for Node and Python that: authenticates, lists available models, makes a single generate request, prints tokens as they stream, and shows a simple fallback path on 429/503.
- Offer a 10–15 minute "guided lab" with checkpoints: install, env var, first call, streaming, and sanity-check evaluation.
- Supply an error-recovery checklist that non-engineer CS reps can follow and that returns structured telemetry tags for triage.

Lab 0: prereqs (for the instructor)
- Have test workspace with an API key (scoped to demo models) and a sandbox account.
- Console route already created: /demo/quickstart (model pinned to small-latency)
- Prepare short-canned prompts that show hallucination vs grounded output.

Minimum Quickstart (Node, 8 lines):
- Steps: npm install @redwood/sdk -> export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx -> node quickstart.js
- quickstart.js should: import client, await client.models.list(), const { stream } = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'small-latency', messages: [...] }); stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk.text)); stream.on('end', () => console.log('
complete'));

Minimum Quickstart (Python, 10 lines):
- pip install redwood-sdk -> export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx -> python quickstart.py
- quickstart.py: from redwood import Redwood; client = Redwood(); print(client.models.list()); r = client.text.generate(model='small-latency', prompt='Translate...'); print(r.output);

Guided Lab: 15-minute flow (script for instructor)
1) 0–2m: Setup & env (confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY var)
2) 2–6m: Run minimal quickstart and inspect console output
3) 6–9m: Show streaming variant (how partial tokens arrive) and how to cancel (client.cancel())
4) 9–12m: Demonstrate function-calling: register simple function (webhook) and show structured JSON in response
5) 12–15m: Trigger a quota/429 by using a simulated rate limit header (explain retry-after) and walk through fallback to a lower-cost model

Error modes & recovery checklist (for triage)
- 401 / missing-key: check env var name (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and workspace binding. Ask user to run: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY (or setx on Windows).
- 403 / permissions: confirm key scope and route (hosted vs dedicated). If Private, check VPN/VPC routing.
- 429 / rate-limited: read Retry-After header; suggest exponential backoff with jitter; in quickstart, show snippet that retries up to 3 times then falls back to model 'small-cost'.
- 503 / transient infra: check status.redwood.com, suggest retry with increasing backoff; capture request-id header and paste it into support ticket.
- Streaming partials drop / broken connection: detect socket EOF and attempt resume via range/KV-cache check (if supported). If no resume: advise restart and surface sample inputs to debug.
- Validation errors (bad JSON for function-calls): return example of well-formed function schema and suggest using the CLI's schema-validate command.

Telemetry & logging guidance (what quickstart should do automatically)
- Emit a single event when quickstart finishes: event.name=quickstart.complete, properties={runtime: node|python, model: _, duration_ms: _, success: true|false, error_class: _}.
- Capture request-id and attach to event (this helps support correlate requests to logs).
- Ship a short sample of the prompt (hash, not raw content) when sending anonymized telemetry.

Quick code snippets (for docs insertion)
- Retry-on-429 pseudocode (language-agnostic)
- Streaming handler example showing partial token print and graceful cancel
- Small fallback policy: on persistent 429 or error, client.call({ model: 'small-cost', prompt: samePrompt }) and log delta in latency/cost

UX copy suggestions (right-sized strings for the console)
- On success: "✅ Connected to Redwood — model small-latency — streaming... press CTRL+C to stop"
- On auth missing: "🔒 No API key found. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and retry. See https://redwood.com/docs/keys"
- On rate limit: "⚠️ Rate limited. Retrying in 3s (attempt 2/3) — fallback available after 3 attempts"

Open questions / items to decide (notes to self)
- Do we pin quickstart to a single canonical model name (small-latency) or detect the fastest available model in the account?
- Should telemetry be opt-in by default or show a short opt-in prompt during quickstart on first run? (privacy/legal ask)
- For Private deployments: do we ship an alternate quickstart that emphasizes custom endpoints and CA cert installation?

Follow-on tasks (owners & rough ETA)
- Copy edits and legal review for telemetry messaging — owner: Priya Nair — ETA: 2026-03-20
- Implement node/python quickstart canonical files in /docs/quickstarts repo — owner: Ethan Brooks — ETA: 2026-03-24
- Add a simple bash/windows powershell script that sets env var and runs the quickstart — owner: Sofia Martinez — ETA: 2026-03-28
- Add automated smoke test in CI that runs the quickstart against a sandbox key and asserts completion event — owner: Marin Alvarez — ETA: 2026-04-06

Appendix: sample troubleshooting ticket template (for CS)
- Steps to reproduce (include exact quickstart file and runtime)
- Copy of error response (headers + body) including request-id
- Duration and network context (VPN, Private deployment, region)
- Did user set proxy or custom CA? (yes/no)
- Attach quickstart log (stderr + telemetry events export)

Notes to self (rough, delete before final)
- Keep labs short — folks drop off after 20m. Stick to 1 core win (live streaming) + 1 safety win (fallback)
- Consider microvideos (30–60s) that show streaming vs batch to reduce friction
- Cross-link to `developer-experience/sdk-first-run-journey-and-templates-draft` (there's overlap; ensure we avoid duplication)

End.
